changelog: Reverts the fbi-based very-early boot splash (v0.15.6-0.15.10) entirely - confirmed on real hardware to cause a multi-minute display hang blocking the clock indefinitely, recoverable only via SSH (fbi does not respond to SIGTERM, requiring a hard SIGKILL after systemd's ~90s stop timeout, on top of the display handoff itself stalling for several more minutes). Kept the one unrelated, still-valid fix discovered along the way: the swaybg splash fallback now references /opt/pinclock/current directly instead of the /home/vfw/pinclock compatibility symlink, which silently drifts stale after OTA updates. IMPORTANT MANUAL CLEANUP REQUIRED on any device that received v0.15.6-0.15.10: this update alone does not remove the already-installed systemd unit or sudoers rule (both live outside the OTA-managed tree) - run: sudo systemctl disable --now pinclock-early-splash.service && sudo rm /etc/systemd/system/pinclock-early-splash.service /etc/sudoers.d/pinclock-early-splash && sudo systemctl daemon-reload
